title: Incremental deploy + fallback playbook (scratch)
content:
Context: quick scratchpad for a small, low-risk incremental deploy of rt-serving v1.12.4-rc2 -> stable; target window next Tue 02:00-05:00 PST. Purpose is an executable checklist + triggers for automated fallback; keeping this as a personal playbook so I can copy into release tickets.

Goals:
- Ramp traffic from 0% -> 100% over ~60 minutes with automated health checks.
- Fail closed: if any critical threshold breaches, revert traffic to last-stable (v1.12.3) and mark for investigation.
- Minimize customer impact and reduce manual interventions.

High-level plan (phases):
1) Preflight (T-48h to T-1h):
   - Smoke tests against staging and a subset of prod-like workloads (long-seq, short-seq, embeddings).
   - Run local perf bench with same instance types: compare p50/p95 token latencies; target p95 <= baseline*1.15.
   - Ensure canary image is pinned: image: ghcr.io/redwood/rt-serving:v1.12.4-rc2
   - Confirm metrics dashboards exist and Alert IDs are known (see linked_artifacts).

2) Canary ramp (0–60m): automated traffic steering via routing-proxy
   - 0% -> 1% (0–5m): baseline health checks: 50 requests/min, golden prompts.
   - 1% -> 5% (5–15m): check error-rate <0.5%, p95 latency < threshold, CPU/GPU mem ok.
   - 5% -> 20% (15–30m): validate token cost and output quality with quick eval set (10 prompts).
   - 20% -> 50% (30–45m): monitor traffic mix; watch cache hit rate drop.
   - 50% -> 100% (45–60m): final ramp if all signals green.

Key metrics (automated):
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) > 0.75% -> trigger rollback.
- p95 latency increase > +300ms absolute OR +40% relative -> rollback.
- Token cost deviation > +25% (unexpected) -> pause and evaluate.
- Quality regressions: BLEU/ROUGE drop on eval set > configured alert -> pause for human review.

Automatic fallback behavior (what routing-proxy does):
- If any of the above metrics cross threshold for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (5m each), rollback to pinned commit: tag v1.12.3-stable.
- Fallback sequence: routing-proxy re-route -> stable-region replica -> notify #deployments slack; create DEPLOY-233 comment + run postmortem template.

Manual escalation steps (if auto-fallback doesn't solve):
- Step 1: Pause cadence, pin traffic to 25% and run heavy profiling (SRE: Drew).
- Step 2: If GPU OOMs or kernel faults, immediately drain new nodes and scale down canary fleet.
- Step 3: If output-quality issue (semantic), rollback and run A/B comparison of prompts vs baseline; revert model IR if needed.

Pre-flight checklist (quick):
- [ ] Canary image built and sha256 verified
- [ ] Post-deploy smoke job in CI passes (smoke-canary pipeline)
- [ ] Dashboards: p50/p95, error rate, cost-per-token, cache-hit-rate, kv-cache-misses
- [ ] Alerts wired to #deployments and PagerDuty
- [ ] Rollback playbook linked in release ticket and owner on-call assigned

Commands/ops snippets (notes to self):
- Pin routing rule: curl -X POST https://routing-proxy/api/rules -d '{"service":"rt-serving","canary":true,"weight":5}' 
  (replace with API key from vault)
- Force rollback (manual): ./tools/traffic-shift --service rt-serving --from canary --to stable --weight 100 --reason "auto-rollback"

Observability tips:
- Use sample IDs to trace both model and pre/post-processing latency. If p95 jumps but CPU is flat, suspect kernel/quantization regressions.
- Watch KV cache warmup: first 10 minutes will show elevated latency until cache hits stabilize.

Notes / open questions (scratch):
- Should we enable 2x smaller batch size for canary to lower tail latencies? pros/cons: reduces throughput but may reduce p95 spikes.
- Who owns the eval-set for embeddings drift checks? Need to confirm with Marco.

Post-mortem stub (if rollback):
- Timeline, earliest symptom, automated triggers, human actions, RCA owner, follow-ups.

Personal reminders:
- Keep this doc concise and copy relevant sections into the release ticket.
- After a successful ramp, update canary runbook with any new thresholds that proved too tight/loose.

End of scratch; will prune and paste into INF-4182 release description once validated.
